title: P01 looped middle: 7 logical blocks over the 6 unique 101-claude blocks (A-B-C-D-D-E-F), same parameters
description: P01 (looped architectures): build the 7-block fork GPT and alias logical block 4 to block 3, so the incumbent's six unique blocks (4,793,856 params, unchanged) run as A-B-C-D-D-E-F with one extra application of the middle block during pretraining, RL and eval. This separates depth from parameters after 102-claude (7 untied blocks, +0.79M params) and 103-claude (6 blocks, +0.79M MLP params) both lost ~-35, and tests whether an iterated middle transformation composes better into >=7-line proofs.
hypothesis: The Lean incumbent reaches its val-loss floor (~0.08) within ~60 s and then only memorizes, so steps are not the constraint; 102 and 103 lost the same ~-35 at +0.79M params with very different step counts, pointing at added unique parameters (more memorization capacity), not depth. Reusing block 3 adds a 7th sequential transformation at fixed unique capacity: if proof steps are compositional, an iterated middle block gives a policy whose per-step competence extrapolates better to >=7-line targets, raising round-1 RL targets solved and the final metric. Unlike 089 (which removed untied blocks and lost -68 via length extrapolation), no untied block is removed here. Risk: the extra compute costs ~14% of steps as in 102 and the repeated block may just act like 102.
expected_delta: -35 to +40 theorems at >=7 (central +3); pretraining ~3,050-3,250 steps (102: 3,114), final val loss 0.080-0.087, held-out greedy >=0.98, total_secs ~1,950-2,050

arch.change: CHANGED vs 101-claude: GPT(vocab, 7, 256, 8) is built and model.blocks[4] is aliased to model.blocks[3] right after construction, so 7 logical block applications run over the same 6 unique blocks (block 3 applied twice in a row); widths, heads, RoPE, LayerNorm, GELU, untied embedding/readout unchanged
arch.n_params_detail: 6 unique blocks 4,738,560 (789,760 each) + emb 27,392 + head 27,392 + ln_f 512 = 4,793,856 (vocab 107), identical to 101-claude; the fork's n_params() sums self.parameters(), which dedupes the aliased block
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: GPT(vocab, 7, 256, 8) from the fork, alias blocks[4] = blocks[3], then load state (the state dict repeats the shared tensors under blocks.3 and blocks.4; loading into an unaliased 7-block GPT gives an identical function). The live harness keeps the aliasing through RL and eval.
arch.kv_cache: unchanged fork code: one cache dict per model.blocks entry, so 7 distinct caches, one per logical application (same aliasing mechanism as 089-claude, which ran cleanly)

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 078-claude except the orthogonalization polynomial)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: CHANGED: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / 256) per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 2 (070-claude: 1), head (99,256) 1. Every Muon update now has element RMS ~1/16 times lr; only fc2's step doubles.
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: All 24 hidden projection parameters (4 per block x 6 blocks) plus head.weight (107,256; vocab 107, no bias) are in Muon: 25 matrices. Six qkv.weight matrices of shape (768,256) use independent Q/K/V updates, represented as a batch of three (256,256) matrices; proj/fc1/fc2 and head are orthogonalized whole. head is wide (107<256) so it is not transposed.
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.
muon.coefficients_note: CHANGED: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: CHANGED: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (incl. ln_f) throughout; head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 21 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3.
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW
optimizer.parameters: All 24 unique hidden projection parameters (4 per block x 6 unique blocks; the aliased block is deduplicated by .parameters()) plus head.weight in Muon: 25 matrices, as in 101-claude. The shared block's gradient is the sum over its two applications.

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)

config.init: Fork default construction of 7 blocks (the discarded 7th block's draws shift the RNG stream vs 101-claude), alias, then orthogonal_ on every unique 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); embedding and readout keep the fork normal(0.02); biases zero.
